values: GP Patient Survey 2025: List of reporting variables CSV label file
This document provides labels to help users interpret the CSV files. If you have any questions about the CSV label file, please email the team at:
The GPPS survey results are available from the surveys and reports section of the website:

This file links the variable names in the CSV files to labels which explain the content. For every question in the questionnaire there are weighted base, count and percentage variables, as well as the unweighted base.

The file for 2025 uses substantive variable names. The first part of each variable name identifies the section of the questionnaire from which the question is drawn. For example, 'localgpservices' refers to the section of the questionnaire called 'Your GP practice services'. The second part of the variable name identifies the individual question. The suffix identifies the nature of the variable e.g. .pct variables are percentages and .count variables are counts.
Further details on the production of evaluative statistics are available in the Presentation of Results:

Two types of suppression are used in GPPS:
•  In cases where a result is based on fewer than 10 people (unweighted), it has been suppressed. For example, where fewer than 10 people answered a question from a particular organisation, the results are not shown.
•  In addition, for organisations with an eligible population of 1,000 or less, individual response option counts below 5 (but excluding 0) and corresponding percentages have been suppressed for the relevant questions in the 'Some questions about you' section and questions relating to long-term conditions, disabilities, or illnesses. In instances where only one response option is suppressed for these questions, the next lowest response option has also been suppressed to prevent back calculation of the primary suppressed result. The Technical Annex contains the full list of questions where this applies.

In the CSV files, the following negative values are used where data has been suppressed:
•  -99 is used for confidence intervals, where they are not available (i.e. where the percentages are suppressed)
•  -98 is used for percentages between 0 and 0.5%
•  -97 is used for suppressed data. 

'Population’ for the GP Patient Survey is defined as the number of patients on the GP registered list for that organisation.  

These suppression methods are used to prevent individuals and their responses being identifiable in the data, and to ensure results based on very small numbers of respondents are not released.
